records.description: NorthLink Aviation LLC is developing a dedicated air-cargo campus on 120 acres at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport under a 55-year state lease. The planned infrastructure includes an approximately 90,000-square-foot warehouse and office complex, an 80-acre aircraft apron, hydrant fueling and ground-service facilities, with an ultimate design of 15 aircraft stands. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III acquired control on November 3, 2021, and the Barings-managed Alaska Future Fund was subsequently disclosed as an owner and co-investor; neither investor's exact percentage is publicly disclosed. The airport is the lessor, not an equity owner. FAA approval and groundbreaking occurred in 2023, but construction remained phased and delayed, with six stands planned by 2027 and no evidence of terminal operations by August 19, 2026. No later financing-driven control transfer, sale or signed pending exit was identified.

records.description: Strategic Venue Partners designs, finances, owns, operates and upgrades neutral-host in-building wireless infrastructure under long-term venue contracts. The platform's assets include distributed antenna systems, public-safety networks, private LTE/CBRS, Wi-Fi and fiber serving healthcare, hospitality, education, entertainment, retail, real-estate and data-center venues. SVP launched in 2017 and formed a holding company in January 2019 to consolidate its infrastructure assets. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund II records 2019 as its entry year and remains the controlling sponsor. Brookfield Asset Management and institutional partners completed a minority equity investment through Brookfield Infrastructure Structured Solutions on December 11, 2024; the exact percentage, security and holding SPVs are not publicly disclosed. A March 2025 refinancing reconfirmed Tiger control and Brookfield's minority position, and no later owner transfer or signed exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

records.description: Summit Carbon Solutions is developing a carbon-dioxide capture, transportation and permanent-sequestration network for ethanol producers in the Midwest. The company is an active development-stage infrastructure platform, but no construction start, full project-finance close or revised commercial-operation date was identified through August 19, 2026. After a 2026 reroute, the current core is focused on Iowa, Nebraska and Wyoming and retains 27 Iowa ethanol plants while removing approximately 200 route miles; the former approximately 2,000-mile, five-state and 20-million-ton annual design should not be treated as the current approved or operating footprint. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III invested in 2021 and remains the qualifying infrastructure owner. TPG Rise Climate contributed $300 million to the 2022 equity raise through a climate-private-equity strategy and is therefore not counted as a qualifying infrastructure-fund owner. Project, pipeline, capture, storage and site LLCs remain subordinate to the single Summit platform.

records.description: Unison Energy, LLC develops, finances, builds, owns, operates and maintains behind-the-meter microgrids and distributed-energy systems for commercial and industrial customers across North America. Its primary model uses long-term energy-service agreements and project SPVs, while the company also supports customer-owned EPC, operations-and-maintenance and hybrid structures; not every system is therefore owned by Unison. The platform serves healthcare, data-center, industrial, hospitality, logistics and other resilience-sensitive facilities using combined heat and power, controls, solar, batteries and thermal systems. At Tiger's June 2024 entry, public materials described approximately 30 operating or signed-ESA projects and about 26 MW installed; a current aggregate scale is not publicly disclosed. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III acquired control through Fund III AIV U LP on June 17, 2024 from American Infrastructure Funds/AIM Universal and Hunt Companies. Exact percentages and consideration were not disclosed, and no later sale or signed ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

records.description: Intermountain Infrastructure Group, LLC develops, owns and operates long-haul and regional fiber networks, offering dark fiber, wavelengths, high-capacity internet and colocation. The U.S.-headquartered platform is building and operating routes across the western and northern United States, with Canada as a secondary market. Its Northern Tier system is a wholly owned multi-conduit route designed to connect the Pacific Northwest with the Minneapolis area, while other routes serve the Inland Northwest and Northern Rockies. Wafra and Post Road announced their investment in February 2023 and completed the recapitalization on January 12, 2024 through WRA II-Pioneer (S) LLC and PRSOF II IIG Inc. Future Standard later succeeded Post Road as manager of the digital-infrastructure platform. IIG identified Wafra as its majority shareholder and Future Standard as its other backer in June 2026; current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

records.description: Mission Clean Energy LLC is a U.S. utility-scale solar and battery-storage development platform headquartered in San Francisco.
